items.title: A service site built for high-intent visitors
items.description: A fast, message-led website that carries the promise from a social post or referral into a focused enquiry path.
items.challenge: A founder earns attention on social, but a generic site makes the offer hard to understand and the next step easy to postpone.
items.approach: Tighten the positioning around one buyer journey, build modular proof and offer sections, and instrument the enquiry path.
items.acceptanceCriterion: A visitor can identify the audience, offer, proof, and next step without guessing.
items.designedOutcome: Make the right prospect understand the offer and trust the next step quickly.

visual.title: One promise. One clear next step.

items.title: A knowledge copilot with human control
items.description: A secure assistant that searches approved business knowledge, drafts useful responses, and shows the source behind every answer.
items.challenge: Support and operations teams search scattered documents, then rewrite the same answers without a reliable source trail.
items.approach: Index only approved knowledge, retrieve cited context, draft within guardrails, and route uncertain answers to human review.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Every draft exposes its sources, and uncertain output routes to review before it can be used.
items.designedOutcome: Cut time spent finding and rewriting information while keeping people in control.

items.title: A decision workspace that surfaces the next move
items.description: A focused analytics product combining operational data, forecasts, and clear explanations instead of another dashboard full of noise.
items.challenge: Operational data exists, but teams discover risk late because dashboards show activity without explaining the next decision.
items.approach: Unify the critical signals, surface forecasts with confidence and drivers, and pair each alert with a clear action.
items.acceptanceCriterion: Every alert pairs data freshness, drivers, and forecast context with a responsible next action.
items.designedOutcome: Help a team notice risk and opportunity early enough to act.

faqs.title: Questions worth asking before you hire any studio.
faqs.subtitle: If an answer affects trust, ownership, cost, or delivery, it should be clear before the project starts.
faqs.contactPrompt: Have a question that is not covered here?

items.question: Can you help us decide what to build first?
items.answer: Yes. A focused discovery or blueprint is often the safest first engagement. We map the problem, users, risks, and smallest useful scope before recommending a full build.

items.question: How do pricing and payment usually work?
items.answer: The Pathfinder ranges are directional. After discovery, we provide a clear scope and milestone-based estimate. Complexity, integrations, data readiness, security, and speed are the biggest variables.

items.question: Can you improve an existing website or product?
items.answer: Yes. We can audit and improve an existing experience, work inside a current codebase, or rebuild only the parts where the expected benefit justifies it.

items.question: Who owns the code, designs, and project accounts?
items.answer: You do after agreed payments are complete. We prefer shared access and client-owned production accounts so the system is portable and the handoff is straightforward.

items.question: How do you handle sensitive data in AI projects?
items.answer: We define what data is allowed, choose suitable providers and retention settings, limit access, add review where needed, and document the flow. Regulated use cases may require specialist legal or security review.

items.question: How will we see progress during the build?
items.answer: Through regular working demos, a shared view of scope and decisions, and direct discussion of blockers or tradeoffs. The cadence is agreed at kickoff.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: Every build includes a defined launch and handoff window. We can also agree on maintenance, monitoring, iteration, or team support when the product needs ongoing care.
